clue.text: Storyteller's introduction to mystery as worker swallows poison

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter, so the first letter of mystery is taken
one piece swallowing another takes it inside, so the poison goes into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: upas is a tree whose sap is a famous poison
an ant is the classic worker insect in crosswords

explanation.surface: A writer's opening to a whodunit, where a labourer gulps down poison.
explanation.walkthrough: The poison goes in after the first letter of 'as'. The 's after Storyteller stands for 'is' and only links the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy de Maupassant was a French writer celebrated for his short stories, hence a storyteller.

clue.text: Most important chap concealing ego

indicators.note: a word concealing another holds it out of sight inside itself

parts.note: a chap is a man
ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: The leading fellow is hiding his self-importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Main means chief or principal, as in the main event.

clue.text: Politician has anger when restricted by American law-enforcers

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in by it, so these pieces sit inside the other

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: An angry politician finds himself constrained by American police.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests police, but the law-enforcers are sports officials who enforce the laws of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials such as cricket or baseball umpires enforce the rules of play, so they are law-enforcers in a sporting sense.

clue.text: I had bumped into Mark, someone on the same side, by chance

indicators.note: one thing bumped into another is pushed inside it here

parts.note: an accent is a mark over a letter
I had contracts to I'd, giving these two letters
an ally is a partner on your side

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they collided with Mark, a teammate, purely by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is an accent mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without intention, happening by luck rather than design, is done in an unplanned way.

clue.text: More irritable photographer at seaside may do this

indicators.note: at places one piece next to the other, the action at the location

parts.note: a photographer snaps pictures, which is what the clue says they may do
a pier is a seaside structure

explanation.surface: A grumpier photographer works the seafront taking holiday pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may do this' points back to the photographer's action, a snap, placed before the seaside pier.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy describes someone short-tempered, and the comparative form means more short-tempered.

clue.text: Foreigner's refusal to accept golfer as national hero

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the golfer goes inside the refusal

parts.note: non is French for no, a foreign refusal
Ernie Els is a South African golfer

explanation.surface: A foreigner's refusal to accept a golfer as a hero of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Horatio Nelson, victor of Trafalgar, is a British naval hero commemorated in London's Trafalgar Square.

clue.text: Experts? They can be worth more than kings and queens

definitions.meaning: an expert at something is a crack performer or virtuoso

definitions.text: They can be worth more than kings and queens
definitions.meaning: in many card games the top card of each suit outranks the king and queen

explanation.definitionFit: Highly skilled people, and the top-ranking playing cards, are both called by this word.

clue.text: Harmony comes with artist — fancy!

parts.note: chime can mean agreement or harmony, as in to chime with
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An exclamation that harmony arrives alongside an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy!' reads as an exclamation of surprise, but is a noun meaning a figment of imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild illusion or fanciful notion, so a fancy in the sense of an imagined thing.

clue.text: Little son, terribly dreary, yet can be very optimistic

parts.note: little signals a shortened form, and S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly treated and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A small boy, though awfully gloomy, can still be hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' is only a link; 'dreary' looks like it describes the boy, but it is part of the anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with stars in their eyes is naively hopeful and idealistic, so very optimistic.

clue.text: Pure rascal, English Conservative with old-fashioned message

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal
a cable is a telegram, now an outdated way to send a message

explanation.surface: A rogue English Tory sends an outmoded telegram while claiming purity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawless, without fault or blemish, is pure in the sense of spotless.

clue.text: Girl from London in Andover

indicators.note: letters taken from a run of words are lifted straight out of it

explanation.surface: A girl comes from London to live in Andover.
explanation.walkthrough: The name spans London, in and Andover; Andover is a town in Hampshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nina is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Somehow he had glitter, being none too serious

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters arrive in some unexplained new order

explanation.surface: He somehow had sparkle, taking things playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carefree and cheerful rather than grave means not taking things too seriously.

clue.text: Hurry back for jazz

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for hurry from right to left

parts.note: to dart is to rush or hurry

explanation.surface: A call to rush back for some jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Trad is short for traditional jazz, the revived New Orleans style.

clue.text: Publicist apt always to make a quick buck

parts.note: PRO is a public relations officer, a publicist
fit means suitable or apt
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A publicist is forever keen to earn fast money.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the verb here, after the link 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: To profit unfairly, especially by exploiting shortages, is to cash in fast at others' expense.

clue.text: Affirms what may be said of subjects

definitions.meaning: to declare or assert something as true

definitions.text: what may be said of subjects
definitions.meaning: in grammar and logic, the part of a sentence that states something about its subject

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means asserts; the grammatical noun is what a sentence says about its subject.

clue.text: Disliked being dispatched into the grass

indicators.note: into signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands
dispatched means sent off

explanation.surface: Someone hated being thrown out into the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To take offence at or feel bitter about something is to dislike it strongly.

clue.text: A few words of adulation one issued about hospital

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the remaining letters go round the hospital letter
something issued has gone out, so the letter for one leaves the word

parts.note: praise is adulation or acclaim
one is the Roman numeral I
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A brief compliment sent out about a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issued' removes I from PRAISE, leaving PRASE, and 'about' wraps that around H.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a short group of words forming a unit, so just a few words.

clue.text: Theologian embraced by explosive king, being cherished

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held inside its arms

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A theologian clasped by a volatile monarch, and much loved.
explanation.walkthrough: DD goes inside HELEAR, after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured and loved fondly is valued greatly, as in 'all that we hold dear'.

clue.text: Frustrate successive characters wanting to have a meal

parts.note: D, E and F are consecutive letters of the alphabet
to eat is to have a meal

explanation.surface: Successive people stymied by their hunger for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is a link here, not a deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat a plan is to thwart or foil it.

clue.text: Female with a new man, we hear? That could mean love letters

indicators.note: we hear says the word for man is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A woman with a new boyfriend, people say: hence the love letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters from admirers to a celebrity are adoring correspondence, a kind of love letter.

clue.text: Fish swimming ashore starts to seem exhausted

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters moving about freely into a new order
the starts of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A fish thrashing towards land begins to look worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges ASHORE into SEAHOR; the starts of seem and exhausted add SE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea horse is a small upright marine fish with a horse-like head.

clue.text: Communist policy establishing absolute boundary

parts.note: red is the traditional label for a communist
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A communist policy sets a firm limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit that must never be crossed is a firm cutoff, an uncrossable limit.

clue.text: Exert to the utmost in race

definitions.meaning: to push something to its limit
a breed or stock of animals or plants

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means push to the limit; the noun means a lineage or breed, a race.

clue.text: Put together record about one outside residence

indicators.note: about means around, so the record's letters go round the rest

parts.note: CD is a compact disc, a record

indicators.note: outside means one piece sits on either side of another

parts.note: a flat is a residence

explanation.surface: Someone compiled a disc about a person outside their home.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two containers here: 'one' wraps the residence, and then the record wraps the result of that.
explanation.definitionFit: To conflate is to combine two or more things into one, to merge them.

clue.text: Helps to make incursions, demolishing front

indicators.note: knocking down the front of a word removes its first letter

parts.note: to raid is to make incursions into territory

explanation.surface: Assistance for launching raids by knocking down a frontline.
explanation.walkthrough: RAIDS loses its first letter, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Assists or supports someone, as a verb in the third person.

clue.text: Loose? Yes and no

parts.note: the word means dissolute, as in a loose living lot, and also firmly fixed, the opposite of slack

explanation.definitionFit: A word with contrary senses: immoral and wild in one, securely stuck and immovable in another.

clue.text: Meal given to thousand people who work together

parts.note: tea is an evening meal in British usage
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Supper is provided for a thousand colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad or crew is a group cooperating on a shared task.

clue.text: Composer wandering in alien parts

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A composer roaming foreign lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was a great Italian Renaissance composer of church music.

clue.text: Strong man falling over, having taken a punch

indicators.note: having taken away a letter removes it from the word
falling over turns the word upside down, read here from the end

parts.note: Atlas was the Titan who held up the heavens, a byword for strength

explanation.surface: A muscleman toppling after being struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling over' turns ATLAS into SALTA, and 'having taken' removes A.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt in the figurative sense is piquancy or zest, the bite or kick that gives something life.

clue.text: Cook determining, having lost heart, what to put in food

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so the letters are falsified into a new order
losing heart means losing the central letter

explanation.surface: A chef decides, after losing courage, what goes in a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost heart' drops M from the middle of DETERMINING, and 'Cook' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: One component of a recipe or dish is something added to the mixture.
